notes: Zul'Farrak (map 209), written from the world database export of tortoise-wow 5d79486 (tools/dungeongen/testdata/zulfarrak, read with export.sh) and the instance script src/scripts/dungeons/zulfarrak. THE ROUTE: Antu'sul (in seven legs), Theka the Martyr, Hydromancer Velratha (1470 yd of navmesh path from the entrance, checked by TestZulfarrakOnNavmesh), then the courtyard of the pyramid and Witch Doctor Zum'rah (PR B, TortoiseBots #984), then the legs after Zum'rah that were written from the instance script and have not run live: the stairs event (stairs, stairs_top, stairs_base), Sergeant Bly and his crew (bly), the End Door (weegli_door) and Chief Ukorz Sandscalp with Ruuzlu (ukorz). A failure in one of them ends the run; from_leg "stairs" starts there. Checked live 2026-10-14: a GM-invisible walk of the whole instance (~3130 yd, 78 walk_path calls, all arrived, no stuck spot, nothing attacked; tests/zf-map/MAP.md in the audit folder). Static spawn positions match the export to the decimal; 59 of the 64 pull-group mobs of the first draft were seen within 10 yd (two road patrollers 12 yd away, three west-road mobs out of the walker's sight); the live walk is why Theka and Velratha are met on their patrol and the patrolling packs have a 30 yd radius.

Left out of this plan: (1) nothing of the Gong's: Gahz'rilla (7273) is in this plan since PR A, as the optional gahzrilla leg (the Gong of Zul'Farrak, 141832, lock 459, is rung by using the Mallet of Zul'Farrak, item 9240, on it; the leg is skipped, never failed, unless the carrier or the lead bot has a Mallet in its bags). (2) The Turtle-custom Farraki Arena wing (map y 1300-1440, z about 0: Zel'jeb the Ancient 62495, Sandfury Ritualists 62500, Champion Razjal 62498 / Juthza 62497 / Kath'zen 62496, farraki_arena.cpp): not on any route here. The legs after Zum'rah (stairs to ukorz) were written from the instance script (src/scripts/dungeons/zulfarrak/instance_zulfarrak.cpp and zulfarrak.cpp) and the world export, and none has run live. THE EVENT ORDER the script gave: any Troll Cage used (go_troll_cage) frees Bly's crew (faction 250) and sends it to the top of the stairs; when Weegli arrives there wave 1 (23 trolls) spawns at the foot of the stairs and runs up in groups of 2, 3, 4, ... every 10 s; 10 s after it is dead wave 2 (24 trolls) does the same; wave 3 (Nekrum Gutchewer 7796, Shadowpriest Sezz'ziz 7275 and five trolls, none with a spawn row) spawns the instant wave 2 is dead and is NOT sent up the stairs, the crew goes down to meet it; when wave 3 is dead the event is over, the crew stands at 1874-1895 1199-1206, and Bly's and Weegli's menus offer their option. Weegli's option sends him to blow the End Door; Bly's option turns him, Raven, Oro and Murta hostile 10 s later (Weegli stays friendly) and sends Weegli too. The plan talks to Weegli first, waits for him to be gone and the door open, then talks to Bly (the weegli_door and bly legs), the order the Wowhead Classic comments advise. Ukorz and Ruuzlu stand behind the door.

No team gate is needed: every mob of the route is hostile to both teams (factions 37, 16 and 107); the friendly NPCs (Sergeant Bly's crew faction 35, Elder Wildmane 15578 faction 35 npc_flags 3 at the gong, the three arena NPCs) are not in any pull group.

The End Door (146084, 1854.5 1142.9 16.1) is shut (state ready, flags 32, seen live) and in the middle of the navmesh route between the graveyard (Zum'rah) and the gong: the navmesh has no doors, so the shortest Theka -> Velratha path (562 yd) walks THROUGH the closed door (a GM did, live; bots would too, a player could not). The Velratha leg therefore starts west of the junction at (1645 909) and goes north by the west road (366 yd from the junction, walked live in 12 hops with no replan); no leg may route through the door, which TestZulfarrakOnNavmesh checks along the whole path. The graveyard (x 1832-1898, y 967-1054, about 70 Shallow Grave chests 128308/128403 with a trap 128972 each) is entered only by the zumrah leg, with the bots' looting off for the whole leg (companions_loot false), and left by the stairs leg, which has it off too; every other leg stays out of it. The ukorz leg is the one that goes through the End Door, after the weegli_door leg has waited for it to open.

Entry: needs TortoiseBots #939 (`cmd enter`). The game has no game_tele inside Zul'Farrak (game_tele 160 "Zul'Farrak" is outside, map 1 at -6801.2 -2893.0 9.0, 28 yd from the portal), so there is no entrance_tele and `.tele name` (game_tele names only) cannot put a bot inside; `.go xyz` moves only the caller; and a bot that stands in area trigger 924 (map 1, centre -6773.5 -2889.8 15.1, radius 20) is not taken in, because the module handles CMSG_AREATRIGGER only from the master (PlayerbotAI.cpp:304, TeleportAction.cpp:41-47) and a headless bot never sends its own. The remote driver therefore walks the party to the portal and sends `.bot cmd enter 924` (entrance_trigger 924, whose areatrigger_teleport row sends to map 209 at 1212.67 842.04 8.93346, o 6.28319, required level 35, which is the plan's entrance); on a module without that order the entry fails and the run says it needs #939. outside_tele "farrak" is a partial match that only game_tele 160 has, for prepare.fresh. Live: a GM's `.go xyz 1212.7 842 8.9 209` made a private instance for the mapping walk; that is not an entry for a bound party.

notes: PR A (zulfarrak events design, TortoiseBots #984), stacked on the Zum'rah PR. The Gong of Zul'Farrak (goober 141832, spawn row 27140 at 1650.91 1171.88 10.9, lock 459, event 2488) needs the Mallet of Zul'Farrak (item 9240, a quest item): the leg is OPTIONAL (optional.item 9240): at its start the run looks for the Mallet in the carrier's and the lead bot's bags (`.bot inv`) and, when neither has it, skips the whole leg (legs[i].result "skipped: no Mallet of Zul'Farrak ..."), never a failure. An honest run has no Mallet; a test gives it with dungeon_run's give_items [{"bot": "lead", "item": 9240}] (a GM `.additem 9240` on that bot at the prepare step, listed in setup_shortcuts). HOW THE GONG IS RUNG (live round 3, 2026-10-15: `cmd open` of the gong, step ok in 47.5 s, no ACK or ERR in the trace, no Gahz'rilla within 30 s): the Mallet is USED ON the gong, it is not a key the gong checks. Item 9240's on-use spell is 11434 ("Gong Zul'Farrak Gong": SPELL_EFFECT_OPEN_LOCK_ITEM, implicit target a game object, target flag object, spell range index 12, cast time index 3); its effect opens the gong (its lock 459 is in Lock.dbc, which is not in the repo, so its type is unread; the core has a Gahz'ridian lock type 15) and the open runs the goober's event 2488 (the spell's effect is the core's EffectOpenLock, which ends in the object's use). So the step is `via_item`: the lead or carrier bot that carries the Mallet gets `cmd use 9240 <bot> entry:141832@1650.9,1171.9,10.9` (TortoiseBots walks it to the object and casts, docs/guides/player-controls.md) and not `cmd open`; the stand is 3.5 yd from the gong (a spell cast and the core's use range need a few yards; the first stand was 6.5 yd away). The step is done by the bot that carries the Mallet, never by the GM agent. Every order of the step is a trace event `object_order` with its ACK or ERR.

THE GRAVES (owner order 2026-10-15: open the graves and kill what comes out before the boss; core research, src/scripts/dungeons/zulfarrak/zulfarrak.cpp and sql/base): the graveyard (x 1832-1898, y 967-1054) holds 40 Shallow Graves, all chests (type 3, loot 8367, gold 18-129). 31 are entry 128403, each with a linked trap 128972 (a TRAP object of radius 0: only the chest's use fires it, walking past does nothing; its spell 10247 'Summon Zul'Farrak Zombies' summons one Zombie 7286 and one Dead Hero 7276 at the grave); 9 are entry 128308 (script go_shallow_grave: the first use summons a Zombie with 65 %, a Dead Hero with 10 %, nothing with 25 %, for 30 s). Zum'rah's in-fight 'Awaken Zul'Farrak Zombie' (spell 10731, EventAI 727103, every 18 s from 1-5 s into the fight) has effect ACTIVATE_OBJECT on a Shallow Grave of entry 128403 within 100 yd of him that is spawned and still unopened (conditions 122 AND 123: loot state ready); so each opened 128403 grave is one cast fewer, and the unopened ones are his adds (a Zombie and a Dead Hero each). Fixed spots: the 31 graves. all 31 are steps of this leg (none is left to his Awaken spell 10731: it activates the nearest unopened grave while any is unopened; the three nearest, 1887.94 1029.08, 1892.57 1006.37 and 1891.60 1023.06, are 22-28 yd from him and are the last batch, g8), in walking order from 1859 1058 (nearest neighbour; every stand is a navmesh point within 4 yd of its grave, reached by a complete path, TestZulfarrakGraveSteps), before the trigger: the carrier bot opens one (loot_object on that exact spawn: `spawn` is the export's gameobject.guid, the open goes by its GUID, range 2 yd), the party fights out what comes out (the driver fights the engaged hostiles until none has fought the party for the quiet time, then the loot wait; the rest gate runs only when a rest line is crossed, no fixed wait per grave) BEFORE the next grave's walk and open, then the next. A resumed run asks `cmd state <guid>` first and skips a grave that is opened already or gone, with a note, so it goes on at the first unopened one. The 9 entry 128308 graves are not opened: Zum'rah's spell does not use them and they only spawn extra mobs. Looting stays off for every other bot (companions_loot false); only the carrier opens graves and only these. The earlier detour via 1854 1055 and 1860 1037 is gone: the stands lead along the graves, and the traps have radius 0. Zombie and Dead Hero packs seen near 1879 1038, 1870 1008 and 1891 1008 (zf-zum2-s2, resumed after a wipe) are NOT spawn rows: the world export has no row of 7286 or 7276 and none of the core's creature spawns in the graveyard, so they are what Zum'rah's spell 10731 and the graves summoned in the attempt before, which stay (the summon spell's duration is long) and are met on the walk to the stand; no pull group is added, the grave steps (before the trigger) are what takes them out. Unverified live: that the Opening spell on a grave fires its linked trap, and how many mobs one opening brings. The run's graves_batch (a fixed size) or graves_ramp (start 2, one more after each batch without a wipe, no growth after the first wipe) regroup the same steps; each batch is one graves-batch: note and a remote.grave_batches record.

Leftover summons (round 3, slot 4 attempt b, trace zf-r3-s4-b): after step 16 eleven Zombies (7286) and Dead Heroes (7276) from graves 13-16 stood idle at 100% hp 12-30 yd from the lead; the carrier's walk to the grave at 1861 1019 woke all of them within 2 s and the party went from 5 alive to 2. leftover_entries makes the driver pull and fight the idle ones within 35 yd of the next batch (before it), of the batch just done (after it) and of the trigger's stand (before the trigger).

Owner 2026-10-15: "the boss opens all the graveyards, and if not all are opened before, they get pulled while they try to kill the boss. There can be 1 or 2 graveyards left but not more." Zum'rah's Awaken Zul'Farrak Zombie (spell 10731, spell_script_target: game object entry 128403 only; his AI script 727103 casts only that) activates an unopened 128403 grave within 100 yd of him; the 128308 graves are not used by it and are not opened. He is friendly (faction 35) until the trigger fires, so the three graves 22-28 yd from him (spawns 27128, 27129, 27132) are opened too, as batch g8 after the far graves: all 31 graves of entry 128403 are opened before the trigger.

Wowhead guide (data; the server script wins): kill each Ward (7785) as it appears (kill_first); his Healing Wave and Shadow Bolt Volley want interrupts, which the bots cannot be ordered to do (no cmd verb); fight him in his room with the whole party in it, not pulled out; the Ward summons the skeletons every 5 s (spell 11088), so once all the graves are open the Ward is the add source. Players confirm that opening and clearing all graves first removes the zombie adds.

Round 4 slot 5 (trace zf-r4-s5b): the module refuses the carrier's cmd open while the carrier is in combat ("The bot is in combat and stopped"), so opening through the summons' fight waits about 20 s per chest for the combat to end. graves_open_by agent has the agent's own invisible GM character open the chests (.go xyz to each stand point, its Opening cast), which does not depend on any bot's combat state. The threat lead (area spells off until the tank holds 4 of 5 engaged hostiles, at most threat_wait_s) ran in every batch but the tank never reached it within 10 s: the healer and the DPS drew the summons. That is the tank's threat on summons (a TortoiseBots tank / area-threat matter), not something this plan or the driver can order; it is left as it is.

The carrier's cmd open retries while the carrier is in combat (zf-r4-s4/s5: the module answers in-combat every ~2 s until the fight ends) cost about 2 minutes per grave step; graves_open_by agent avoids them. Wowhead says nothing of a formation either.

THE PHASE CHECK (missing vocabulary, 2026-10-20). The pyramid phase is instance data 1, not 0: Tortoise's `EVENT_PYRAMID = 1` (zulfarrak.h) and `GetData(1)` returns `PyramidPhase`, while `GetData(0)` returns 0 (instance_zulfarrak.cpp). The phase values are NOT_STARTED 0, CAGES_OPEN 1, ARRIVED_AT_STAIR 2, WAVE_1 3, PRE_WAVE_2 4, WAVE_2 5, PRE_WAVE_3 6 (wave 3 is spawned in this case), WAVE_3 7 (5 s later, the crew moves to the foot) and KILLED_ALL_TROLLS 8, so 7 is the value this leg ends on. The agent's driver cannot read it: its `wait_for` holds on units, objects and hostiles only, so for the agent this leg waits on the observable proxy (Nekrum 7796, summoned with wave 3 at phase 6, seen at the foot); that is correct while wave 3 is alive or about to spawn, but a resumed run that starts the leg after wave 3 is dead sees no Nekrum and fails the wait at 600 s. The TortoiseBots run leader CAN read it (2026-10-21, feat/zf-full-module-plan): its loader takes a `hold` done by instance data with flag 8 alone (no encounter flag 32) and any param, and ends the hold when the data reads exactly that value (DungeonRunPolicy.h HoldDoneNote).
